title: RBAC vs ABAC vs PBAC vs ReBAC
subtitle: Four models, one comparison, no hype
content:
👥 RBAC: Roles as Indirection

Role-based access control grants permissions to roles, users to roles. alice is analyst → analyst may read reports. Cheap to start, and it collapses under role explosion: analyst-eu, analyst-us, analyst-eu-manager-readonly… each new dimension multiplies roles until nobody can audit who can do what.

🏷️ ABAC: Attributes Decide

Attribute-based access control evaluates attributes of subject, resource, action, and environment: allow if subject.dept == resource.dept AND clearance >= 3 AND 09:00 < now < 17:00. Far more expressive — and the rules have to live somewhere. Without a policy engine, ABAC becomes stringly-typed if-statements again.

📜 PBAC: The Delivery Mechanism

PBAC is not a rival to RBAC/ABAC — it is how you deliver them. RBAC role mappings, ABAC attribute rules, and ownership checks all become versioned policies evaluated at a PDP. The model answers what logic; PBAC answers where it lives, how it ships, and how it is tested.

🕸️ ReBAC: Relationships Decide (Zanzibar)

Relationship-based access control, pioneered by Google Zanzibar and open-sourced as OpenFGA, stores relationship tuples (anne is editor of doc:Q3) and answers does a path exist from subject to object through allowed relations? Ideal for sharing graphs (docs, repos, drives). Concentric inheritance (editor implies viewer) removes whole classes of tuples.

⚖️ Choosing Honestly

  • Small internal tool, 3 roles, no sharing: RBAC in a policy file is fine. Do not buy a platform.
  • Multi-tenant SaaS with per-customer rules: ABAC-over-PBAC (OPA/Cedar); tenant and attributes in every decision.
  • Drive/Docs-style sharing, teams, nested groups: ReBAC (OpenFGA); graphs beat attribute lists.
  • Data warehouse with masking + row filters: Immuta-style data policies; column tags, not app code.
  • Enterprise with auditors and hundred-app sprawl: PlainID-style orchestration; one policy plane, many enforcement points.

Most real estates end up hybrid: ReBAC for the sharing graph, ABAC-over-PBAC for API/fine-grained rules, data policies for the warehouse. This course teaches all three seams.

questions.question: A company has 400 roles including analyst-eu-readonly-contractor and manager-us-write-fulltime. What is this failure called?

options.text: Role explosion — dimensions multiplied into unauditable roles
Privilege creep on a single account
A secure default-deny posture
Proper separation of duties

questions.explanation: RBAC scales by role count. Every new dimension (region × seniority × employment type) multiplies roles. The fix is attribute/policy rules that compute access instead of enumerating it.

questions.question: allow if subject.clearance >= resource.classification AND subject.dept == resource.dept. Which model?

options.text: ABAC — decision from subject/resource/environment attributes
RBAC — decision from role membership only
ReBAC — decision from relationship graph paths
DAC — decision by object owner discretion only

questions.explanation: Attribute rules over subject, resource, and environment are the textbook ABAC shape. RBAC would need a pre-built role per (dept × classification) combination.

questions.question: How does PBAC relate to RBAC and ABAC?

options.text: PBAC is the delivery mechanism: RBAC/ABAC logic expressed as versioned policy evaluated at a PDP
PBAC replaces both and they must never be used
PBAC is only for networks, RBAC/ABAC only for apps
They are competing vendors and cannot be combined

questions.explanation: Model = what logic. PBAC = where it lives and how it ships. A Cedar permit keyed on a role attribute IS RBAC delivered through PBAC.

questions.question: A docs app needs: anne shared doc:Q3 with team:eng as editors; every editor must read as viewer without extra tuples. Best fit?

options.text: ReBAC (OpenFGA): editor relation implies viewer; team membership resolves transitively
Pure RBAC with one global editor role
A firewall allowlist of IP addresses
Column masking in the warehouse

questions.explanation: Sharing graphs with transitive membership and concentric relations are exactly the Zanzibar/OpenFGA sweet spot. Roles cannot express per-object sharing; ABAC lists get unwieldy.

questions.question: A 3-role internal tool with no sharing and no auditors asks for an enterprise policy platform. Honest advice?

options.text: RBAC in a versioned policy file is enough; do not buy a platform yet
Deploy all five platforms taught in this course immediately
Skip authorization entirely at this scale
Hard-code checks in each handler for speed

questions.explanation: Proportionality is a professional skill. PBAC discipline (default-deny, versioned rules, tests) pays off at any size; the heavy platforms earn their keep with scale, sharing graphs, or audit pressure.

questions.question: A role matrix has 12 regions × 4 seniorities × 3 contract types = 144 roles. What single change kills the explosion?

options.text: Replace the region/seniority/type dimensions with attributes evaluated in policy
Rename roles to shorter codes
Merge everything into one admin role
Move the matrix to a spreadsheet

questions.explanation: Explosion is multiplicative dimensions. Attributes compute what roles enumerate — 3 attributes replace 144 roles.

questions.question: Contractors may read only public documents during business hours. How many new roles does the ABAC version need?

options.text: Zero — one rule over employment-type, classification, and time attributes
One per contractor
One per document
Three — one per condition

questions.explanation: ABAC scales by rule, not by role count. Conditions compose inside one rule.

questions.question: Alice shares doc:Q3 with Bob as viewer; the whole team:eng edits it. How does the team get viewer access with zero per-doc writes?

options.text: Model-level rule (editor implies viewer) plus the team tuple — no per-doc writes
Email everyone a share link
Make all documents public
Copy Bob's tuple to each teammate by hand

questions.explanation: ReBAC puts the implication in the model (concentric relations) and membership in tuples. Per-doc grants are the RBAC reflex this model replaces.
